tasks.title: Đi chơi cuối tuần
tasks.q: Which of these weekend activities do you like?
tasks.open: Let's talk about weekend activities. I really like going to the cinema, because I love films. Do you like going to the cinema?
turns: I don't play football, but I like watching it on TV. What about you? Do you like playing football?
Shopping is OK, but it can be expensive. Do you often go shopping at the weekend?
I visit my grandparents every Sunday. They live near the sea. What about your family?
Sometimes I just stay at home and read a book. Do you like staying at home?
tasks.decide: So, which activity do you like best? I think the cinema is the best. And you?

tasks.title: Quà sinh nhật cho bạn
tasks.q: Which present is best for a friend's birthday?
tasks.open: Let's choose a birthday present for our friend. A book is a nice present, I think, because she likes reading. What do you think?
turns: A T-shirt is nice too, but maybe it's difficult to choose the right size. Do you agree?
Everybody likes cake! We can make it at home, so it's cheap. What do you think about a cake?
A concert ticket is exciting, but it's expensive. Is that a good idea, do you think?
A plant is pretty and it lives a long time. Do you like giving plants as presents?
tasks.decide: So, which present shall we choose? I like the concert ticket best. What about you?

tasks.title: Cách học tiếng Anh
tasks.q: What is the best way to learn English?
tasks.open: Let's talk about learning English. I like watching films in English, because it's fun. Do you watch films in English?
turns: Reading books is good for new words, but it's sometimes boring for me. Do you like reading in English?
I use an app every day on the bus. It's easy. What do you think about apps?
Talking to friends is great, but my friends don't speak English. What about your friends?
Classes are useful because the teacher can help you. Do you go to English classes?
tasks.decide: So, what is the best way, do you think? For me, it's watching films. What about you?

tasks.title: Chuyến đi của câu lạc bộ
tasks.q: A youth club is planning a day trip. Which place would be best?
tasks.open: OK, shall we start with the museum? I think it could be interesting, but some young people might find it a bit boring. What do you think?
turns: The beach would be relaxing, especially in summer. But if the weather is bad, there's nothing to do. Would you agree?
A theme park is really exciting, though the tickets are usually quite expensive. How do you feel about that?
I like the idea of a national park. They could go walking and learn about nature at the same time. What's your opinion?
A big city has lots of things to do, but it can be crowded and tiring. Do you think it's a good choice?
tasks.decide: So, we need to decide. Which place do you think would be the best for the club? I'm thinking the national park.

tasks.title: Sống khoẻ hơn
tasks.q: How can students have a healthier lifestyle?
tasks.open: Let's start with sport. I think doing sport is really important, because it helps you stay fit and meet people. Do you agree?
turns: Eating better is a good idea too, but healthy food can be more expensive. What do you think?
Lots of students don't sleep enough because they stay up late. Do you think sleeping more would help?
Using phones less is difficult for most people, me too! Is it really that important, in your opinion?
Walking to school is easy and free, but it depends on how far you live. What do you think about that one?
tasks.decide: OK, so which one do you think would make the biggest difference? I'd say sleeping more.

tasks.title: Quà chia tay cô giáo
tasks.q: A teacher is leaving the school. Which present should the class give her?
tasks.open: Shall we talk about flowers first? They're nice, but they don't last very long. What do you think?
turns: A photo book is a lovely idea, because it would help her remember the class. Do you like that one?
A watch is a useful present, but it might be too expensive for the class. What's your opinion?
Taking her out for dinner could be fun, but it might be hard to find a time for everyone. Do you agree?
A video message is quite personal, and everyone could say something. How do you feel about that?
tasks.decide: So, which present do you think is the best? I think I'd choose the photo book.

tasks.title: Thành phố đáng sống
tasks.q: What makes a city a good place to live?
tasks.open: Shall we start with public transport? I'd say it's essential, because without it people spend hours in traffic. Wouldn't you agree?
turns: What about parks and green spaces? Personally, I think they're underrated. They make a huge difference to people's mental health. What's your view?
Job opportunities are obviously important, although I suppose they're the reason cities get so overcrowded. How do you see it?
The cost of housing worries me the most. In many cities young people simply can't afford to live near their work. Do you think that's a major factor?
And cultural activities, like concerts and museums. They're nice to have, but are they really essential, in your opinion?
tasks.decide: Now we need to decide which of these is the most important. I'm torn between transport and housing. Which would you choose?

tasks.title: Công nghệ và giới trẻ
tasks.q: How has technology changed the lives of young people?
tasks.open: Let's begin with friendships. In my opinion, social media has made it easier to stay in touch, but perhaps the friendships are less deep. What do you think?
turns: Education has definitely changed. You can learn almost anything online now, which is amazing. Do you think it's made students more independent?
When it comes to free time, I feel young people spend far too long on screens instead of going out. Would you agree with that?
Health is an interesting one. There are fitness apps, but people also sit down much more than before. What's your opinion?
And family life. I've noticed families sitting together but all looking at their phones. Do you think technology has brought families closer or pushed them apart?
tasks.decide: So, which area do you think has changed the most? I'd probably say free time. What about you?

tasks.title: Bảo vệ môi trường
tasks.q: What can people do to protect the environment?
tasks.open: Why don't we start with plastic? It seems like the easiest change to make, because there are so many alternatives now. Do you agree?
turns: Cycling instead of driving sounds great, but in a hot, busy city it isn't always realistic. How do you feel about it?
Eating less meat is supposed to have a big impact, although a lot of people find it hard to change their diet. What do you reckon?
I really like the idea of buying second-hand clothes and furniture. It saves money as well. Have you ever tried it?
Saving energy at home, like turning off lights and air conditioning, is simple but people forget. Do you think it makes much difference?
tasks.decide: Right, we have to agree on which action would have the greatest effect. I'm inclined to say eating less meat. What's your view?

tasks.title: Thành công trong công việc
tasks.q: What factors contribute most to success at work?
tasks.open: Perhaps we could start with qualifications. I'd argue they matter less than they used to, since employers increasingly look at practical skills. Would you go along with that?
turns: Personality is a fascinating one. Someone who's easy to work with often gets further than someone who's simply brilliant. Do you think that's fair?
Contacts, of course, can open doors, although it does raise questions about equal opportunities. Where do you stand on that?
I'm not sure people like to admit the role luck plays. Being in the right place at the right time can make all the difference. What's your take on it?
And hard work, which everyone claims is the key. But surely it isn't enough on its own, is it?
tasks.decide: We need to decide which factor is the most significant. I'm leaning towards personality, but I could be persuaded otherwise. What would you say?

tasks.title: Du lịch và người dân địa phương
tasks.q: How does tourism affect local communities?
tasks.open: Shall we kick off with the economy? On the face of it, tourism brings jobs and money, but much of the profit may go to international companies. What do you make of that?
turns: As for traditional culture, there's a risk that it becomes a kind of performance for visitors rather than something people genuinely live. Would you agree?
The environmental impact can be considerable, particularly in places that weren't built for large numbers of visitors. How serious do you think that is?
Housing is becoming a real issue, with apartments turned into holiday rentals and prices rising for local residents. Have you come across that?
Then there are local services, like transport and hospitals, which can be stretched to the limit in peak season. Do you think tourists should pay more towards them?
tasks.decide: So, overall, which of these effects do you think is the most damaging? I'd probably single out housing. How about you?

tasks.title: Vì sao khó đổi thói quen
tasks.q: Why do people find it difficult to change their habits?
tasks.open: Let's start with lack of time. It's the excuse everyone uses, but I suspect it's often more about priorities than time itself. What's your feeling?
turns: Social pressure is powerful too. If all your friends eat junk food, it's hard to be the one ordering a salad. Does that ring true for you?
Comfort is probably underestimated. Old habits feel safe, even when we know they're bad for us. Would you go along with that?
Not seeing results quickly is a big one for me. When progress is slow, it's tempting to give up altogether. Have you ever experienced that?
And fear of failure. Some people would rather not try than try and fail. Do you think that's the deepest reason?
tasks.decide: Which of these do you think is the main obstacle? I keep coming back to not seeing results. What would you choose?

tasks.title: Phát triển và giữ di sản
tasks.q: How should a city balance development with protecting its heritage?
tasks.open: Shall we begin with old buildings? I'd contend that preserving them is about more than nostalgia; they give a city its character. Though I appreciate that's easy to say if you don't have to live in one. Where do you stand?
turns: New infrastructure is clearly indispensable, but there's a tendency to bulldoze first and ask questions later. Is that an unfair characterisation?
Tourism complicates things, doesn't it? The very heritage that attracts visitors can be eroded by their sheer numbers. How would you reconcile those two pressures?
Local residents often seem to be the last people consulted, which strikes me as rather perverse. Do you think they should have a decisive say?
And public spaces. Squares and markets arguably do more for community life than any single monument. Would you agree, or is that overstating it?
tasks.decide: If the city could prioritise only one of these, which should it be? I'm inclined to say local residents, since everything else follows from their needs. Would you concur?

tasks.title: Trí tuệ nhân tạo
tasks.q: What are the implications of artificial intelligence for society?
tasks.open: Let's take employment first. The prevailing fear is mass unemployment, but historically technology has created as many jobs as it has destroyed. Are you persuaded by that argument?
turns: In education, the question isn't whether students will use these tools, but how teaching adapts to them. What's your take?
Creativity is the one people feel most protective about. I'm not convinced a machine can be creative in any meaningful sense. Would you go along with that, or is that a somewhat romantic view?
Privacy worries me far more, to be honest. These systems depend on vast amounts of personal data. Do you think the trade-off is worth it?
And decision-making: should a machine ever have the final say on, say, medical treatment? Where would you draw the line?
tasks.decide: Which of these do you think will prove the most significant in the long run? My instinct says privacy, but I'm open to persuasion.

tasks.title: Vì sao khó rời công việc
tasks.q: Why do some people find it hard to switch off from work?
tasks.open: Perhaps we should start with technology. Being permanently reachable has blurred the line between work and home, wouldn't you say?
turns: Job insecurity is another factor. If you think your position is precarious, you're hardly going to ignore an email at ten at night. Does that resonate with you?
Workplace culture plays a huge part. In some offices, leaving on time is practically seen as a lack of commitment. Have you encountered that?
Personal ambition is a more delicate matter, because people choose it. Is it fair to see it as a problem at all?
And financial pressure, which often leaves people with no choice but to take on extra work. Is that the most compelling explanation, do you think?
tasks.decide: So which would you single out as the root cause? I'd be tempted to say workplace culture, since it shapes so much of the rest.
